name: THE CLARION OFFICE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE TYPE CASE
LOOK_AT: Lead type in wooden trays. The B is worn nearly flat.
The exclamation marks have a compartment of their own, and it is the largest.
Every letter is cast backward so that it prints forward. It is the most honest thing in the building and it does it in reverse.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It is lead and it has nothing to add.
A faint rattle of lead when the press starts. The type knows what is coming.
Nothing. Several thousand words in that case, and not one of them in order.

overrides.PICK_UP: The letter B, I notice, is nearly worn out. My name has been spending it.

subjects.name: THE PRESS
LOOK_AT: A flatbed press of considerable age, operated by a man of considerable enthusiasm.
A sheet is half-printed in the bed: CONSOLATION REJOICES. The headline has not yet decided at what.
It is older than the town. It came over the mountains in pieces, which is more effort than anyone has put into the news since.
LISTEN_TO: It knocks on the return stroke. It has been knocking for years and it will not be attended to.
The knock again, on the return. I could find it in a minute, and he would print that I had broken it.
A long iron sigh as the bed comes home, and then the knock, with the timing of a man repeating a joke.

overrides.USE: Frame offered to let me. Then he described the last man's sleeve. I withdrew the request and he printed that I had.
overrides.TALK_TO: It has told more of this town's story than anyone alive, most of it invented. I keep my remarks neutral.

subjects.name: BACK EDITIONS
LOOK_AT: Twelve years of the *Clarion*. The Mott story runs on the front page of one issue in three, and has for twelve years, with nothing new in it.
Each Mott story gives a different date for the strike. The latest has moved it to a Sunday, for color.
The oldest are yellow and the newest are white, and the story inside them has not aged at all.
LISTEN_TO: Paper. Rather a lot of it.
The stack creaks. Twelve years of news, settling under its own weight.
Nothing. Yesterday's paper has nothing to add to yesterday.

overrides.PULL: The stack is structural. Frame's filing system is masonry.

subjects.name: THE MOTT PHOTOGRAPH
LOOK_AT: The only known likeness of Obadiah Mott. I have seen this exact photograph in Mr. Sheng's window, advertising collars.
He has the look of a man who was asked to think of something noble and is thinking of lunch.
The photographer's stamp has been trimmed off the bottom, neatly. Somebody wanted this to be a picture of someone.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It is a picture of a man in Ohio.
Nothing. Whoever he is, he has not said a word in twelve years.
The frame ticks on its nail. It is the most this likeness has ever said.

subjects.name: FRAME'S DESK
LOOK_AT: A desk under a drift of proofs, notes and half-sentences. Somewhere beneath them, I am assured, is a desk.
A card pinned to the top reads VERIFY. It has been there so long the ink has faded to a suggestion.
Every drawer is open. Nothing in this office has ever been kept back from print, including several things that should have been.
LISTEN_TO: Paper, shifting whenever the press runs. The desk is in a permanent state of mild landslide.
A pencil rolling slowly toward the edge. It has done this before, and nobody has stopped it.
Nothing, for once. The quietest place in the building is where he does his thinking, which may explain the paper.

subjects.name: THE INK
LOOK_AT: A keg of printer's ink, black as a creditor's mood and nearly as hard to get off the hands.
There are black thumbprints on everything in this office, including, somehow, the ceiling.
The keg is stenciled ST. LOUIS. The news here is local; the black is imported.
LISTEN_TO: A thick, slow settle when the floor moves. It does not slosh. It considers.
Nothing. It is waiting to be turned into opinions.
The lid comes up with a reluctant kiss. I put it back down.

subjects.name: THE SPIKE
LOOK_AT: A paper spike, loaded to the hilt with stories that did not run. It is the most accurate archive in the building.
The top sheet reads CORRECTION in capitals, and nothing else. It was spiked before he could think of one.
He spikes his own stories when better ones occur to him. The better ones are on the front page. The true ones are here.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. A spike is where a story's life ends, and it is very quiet there.
Paper stirring when the door opens. The rejected, briefly hopeful.
Nothing. I will not be adding to it.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW
LOOK_AT: The front window, lettered THE CLARION in gold, backward from in here, which is how Frame sees most things.
People stop outside to read the headline board, then glance in to see whether Frame has noticed them reading. He always has.
The glass is the cleanest thing in the office. He likes to see who is coming before they can deny it.
LISTEN_TO: Main Street, and over it someone reading a headline aloud to someone who cannot read. Both of them are pleased.
The bell over the door, waiting. It rings for news and for creditors and cannot tell them apart.
Boots on the boardwalk, slowing at the glass. Everybody slows here. It is the only place in town the news is free.

subjects.name: THE SCHEDULE BOARD
LOOK_AT: The stage schedules, chalked: arrivals, departures, and a column headed DELAYED that has never once been empty.
One departure has been rubbed out with a thumb. Whoever left on it, Frame is keeping for himself.
The coach east runs Tuesdays. The coach west runs when it feels it has something to say.
LISTEN_TO: Chalk dust drifting off the ledge. Every departure leaves a little behind.
Nothing. A timetable is a silent form of optimism.
The board knocks against the wall when the press runs, in time with it. The whole building keeps the same bad rhythm.

overrides.CLOSE: Tomorrow's headline is chalked and facing the street. There is no closing the news. I have asked.

IGNATIUS FRAME.PICK_UP: He would print it. He would print it on the front page, and he would spell it GRUBBE.
IGNATIUS FRAME.PUSH: He is already leaning toward the next sentence. He does not need help.
IGNATIUS FRAME.USE: Everybody in town uses him. He calls it circulation.
IGNATIUS FRAME.GIVE: Anything I hand him becomes a story. I am being careful what I hand him.
